# Error Handling Requirements for Todo List Backend Service

## Introduction

Robust error handling is essential for the reliability and user trust of the Todo List backend service. The system SHALL ensure every failure, unexpected input, or system error is managed in a manner that preserves user data integrity and provides clear, actionable guidance. All user-facing error responses must be designed with clarity, politeness, and practicality, never exposing technical internals and always helping users move forward or recover.

## Error Scenarios

### 1. Input Validation Errors
- WHEN a user submits a todo item without all required fields (such as an empty title), THE system SHALL block the creation or update and display an explicit message indicating the missing field(s).
- WHEN a user enters data that exceeds allowed limits (such as a title longer than 255 characters), THE system SHALL reject the change and state exactly which limit was violated.
- WHEN a user input does not match the required format (such as a due date in a non-date format), THE system SHALL display a message explaining the correct format and highlight the erroneous entry.

### 2. Authentication and Authorization Errors
- WHEN an unauthenticated user attempts to perform any action involving reading, creating, updating, or deleting todos, THE system SHALL refuse the action and present a clear message that login is required.
- WHEN a user tries to change or remove a todo they do not own, THE system SHALL prevent this action and inform them that they lack permission for that todo item.
- WHEN a logged-in session or authentication token has expired or becomes invalid, THE system SHALL demand re-authentication and explain that login must be renewed.

### 3. Data Operation Errors (CRUD)
- WHEN the backend fails to persist changes (creating, updating, or deleting a todo item) due to any network or server-side error, THE system SHALL show a non-technical, reassuring message asking the user to retry later.
- WHEN an attempt is made to access, update, or delete a todo that no longer exists, THE system SHALL inform the user that the item cannot be found or might already have been deleted.
- WHEN the system receives any unexpected or unclassified backend error, THE system SHALL provide a generic, polite message assuring the user that the issue is recognized and being addressed.

### 4. System and Service-Level Failures
- WHEN any unexpected internal error is encountered, THE system SHALL log necessary diagnostic information (never exposing details to the user) and display a generic apologetic message with next steps.
- WHEN the service experiences downtime or is unreachable, THE system SHALL inform users of the outage, provide information on expected resolution if available, and suggest contact options for support.

## User-Facing Error Messages

### Principles for Error Messaging
- THE system SHALL always use clear, plain, and courteous language in every error message.
- THE system SHALL avoid all technical jargon, error codes, or stack traces in user displays.
- THE system SHALL ensure every error prompt includes guidance on corrective action or what to do next.

### Example Error Messages
| Scenario                                      | User Message Example                                |
|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Missing title                                 | "Please enter a title for your todo item."          |
| Title too long                                | "The title must be 255 characters or fewer."        |
| Bad due date format                           | "The due date must be a valid date."                |
| Not logged in                                 | "You need to log in to perform this action."        |
| Permission denied                             | "You do not have permission to modify this todo."   |
| Session expired                               | "Your session has expired. Please log in again."    |
| Save failed                                   | "Could not complete your request. Try again later." |
| Todo deleted/not found                        | "This todo could not be found or may have been removed."|
| Unhandled error                               | "Something went wrong. We're working on the issue." |
| Service unavailable                           | "The service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again soon."|

## Recovery Actions and User Guidance

### Automated Recovery
- WHEN a temporary error (such as a network failure) is detected, THE system SHALL enable the user to retry the most recent action from where they left off.
- WHEN a validation error occurs, THE system SHALL visually indicate the specific field in error and permit prompt correction.

### User Guidance Steps
- WHEN authentication or permission failures happen, THE system SHALL direct the user either to log in or contact support, as applicable.
- WHEN a todo cannot be found during update or deletion, THE system SHALL instruct the user to refresh their list or review recent changes to their data.
- FOR persistent or unfamiliar errors, THE system SHALL supply direct access to help resources, documentation, or contact info for technical support.

### Support and Escalation
- WHEN a user experiences repeated, unresolved errors, THE system SHALL offer an option to contact support (such as email or a support form) directly from the error display.
- THE system SHALL display an error reference code or unique ID for severe or generic faults to facilitate faster support response.

## Mermaid Diagram: Error Handling Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Action (Create/Update/Delete/Read Todo)"] --> B{"Valid Input?"}
  B -->|"Yes"| C{"Authenticated?"}
  B -->|"No"| D["Show Validation Message"]
  C -->|"Yes"| E{"Operation Successful?"}
  C -->|"No"| F["Show Authentication/Permission Error"]
  E -->|"Yes"| G["Confirm Success to User"]
  E -->|"No"| H{"Known Error?"}
  H -->|"Yes"| I["Show User-Friendly Error Message"]
  H -->|"No"| J["Show Generic System Error, Log Details"]
```

## Success Criteria for Error Handling

- All error cases and scenarios are explicitly handled such that no operation leaves the user without feedback or corrective guidance.
- All error messages are written in courteous, jargon-free, and direct language and include information about next steps for the user.
- No internal error codes, stack traces, or technical data are ever visible to the user.
- The system provides a clear path for recovery, including retry actions or correction guidance as soon as possible after any failure.
- All error conditions are logged internally with sufficient detail for diagnostics but with no leakage of user or system security data.
- Each requirement follows EARS format or natural language statement and is directly actionable for backend implementation.
- All requirements, diagrams, and guidance meet production-level quality, providing backend developers with a complete, ambiguity-free specification for every aspect of error handling in the Todo List backend service.

files.reason: To document key business rules and validation criteria required for the todo item domain.
keyQuestions: What makes a valid todo?
What fields are required or optional?
files.content:
# Minimal Todo List Application Requirements Analysis

## Introduction & Purpose
The Minimal Todo List is a software service that allows individual users to manage a private, personal list of actionable tasks called "todos." This document describes, in precise business language, every requirement, rule, and process flow for creating, updating, completing, and deleting todos. The purpose is to define the minimum necessary requirements for a classic todo app, ensuring zero ambiguity and providing backend developers with a blueprint for compliant implementation—without any unnecessary features or technical design detail.

## Business Requirements & User Interactions
- WHEN a registered user signs in, THE system SHALL allow creation, update, completion status change, and deletion of their own todos.
- WHEN the user is not authenticated, THE system SHALL deny access to all todo operations.
- WHEN the user attempts to access, update, or delete a todo not belonging to them, THE system SHALL deny the action and provide a clear error message.
- THE user SHALL NOT access or interact with any other user's todos.
- WHEN a registered user requests their list of todos, THE system SHALL deliver only their own items.

## Business Rules & Validation
All requirements below follow EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax):

### Core Principles
- WHEN a user creates a todo, THE system SHALL assign ownership to the creator and restrict access to that user only.
- IF a user attempts to access, modify, or delete a todo not owned by them, THEN THE system SHALL deny with "You do not have permission to perform this action."
- Each todo SHALL represent a single actionable task (avoid compound actions).
- WHEN a todo is deleted, THE system SHALL ensure it cannot be retrieved later.

### Field Constraints (applies to all input and update actions)
- WHEN a user submits a new todo, THE system SHALL require a non-empty `title` (1–100 chars, trimmed, no leading/trailing spaces).
- WHEN a user submits a new todo, THE system SHALL require `isCompleted` (boolean).
- WHERE `description` is provided, THE system SHALL accept up to 1,000 characters.
- WHERE `dueDate` is provided, THE system SHALL require it is on or after creation date and not before current date.
- IF `dueDate` provided is in the past, THEN THE system SHALL reject with "Due date must not be in the past."
- IF required fields are missing, THEN THE system SHALL reject the request, indicating all missing fields.

### Field Rules on Update
- WHEN a user updates a todo, THE system SHALL validate user ownership.
- WHERE `title` is updated, THE system SHALL require non-empty string ≤100 chars.
- WHERE `description` is updated, THE system SHALL allow up to 1,000 chars.
- WHERE `dueDate` is updated, THE system SHALL allow only ISO8601 dates not earlier than the todo's creation date.
- WHERE `isCompleted` is updated to true, THE system SHALL auto-set `completedAt` (readonly by user) to the current datetime.
- WHEN reverting from completed to incomplete, THE system SHALL clear `completedAt`.
- IF update request contains no changes, THE system SHALL reject the update.

### Integrity and Lifecycle Constraints
- WHEN a user deletes a todo, THE system SHALL remove only that item and NOT any others.
- Once deleted, THE todo SHALL not be recoverable by any means.
- System-managed fields (`completedAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `id`, `userId`) SHALL be readonly to users, always set or updated only by the system.

### Completion Status Handling
- WHEN a user marks a todo as completed, THE system SHALL set `completedAt` to UTC now.
- IF already completed and marked again, THE system SHALL treat as idempotent and return success.
- IF reverted to incomplete, THE system SHALL set `completedAt` to null.
- WHEN a non-owner attempts to update `isCompleted`, THE system SHALL deny the operation.

### General Validation Logic
- THE system SHALL trim whitespace from `title` and `description` before storing.
- THE system SHALL reject non-boolean `isCompleted` values, or empty/whitespace titles.
- THE system SHALL respond to all rule violations with user-friendly error messages as above.

## Authentication & Authorization Model
- All users must REGISTER and AUTHENTICATE prior to any todo operations.
- Only the AUTHENTICATED user may create, see, complete, update, or delete their own todos.
- THE system SHALL deny unauthenticated requests.
- Each todo is strictly PRIVATE to its creator—no sharing or delegation.
- No user or role other than the owner may see or operate on a todo.

### Session Management
- WHEN a user is authenticated, a session SHALL be created and remain valid for a secure, pre-defined period or until manual logout.
- WHEN the session expires or is logged out, all todo operations are denied.

## Minimal User Flows
### Todo Creation
1. User logs in.
2. User submits `title` (required), `description` (optional), `dueDate` (optional), `isCompleted` (required, default false).
3. System validates all fields and business rules as above.
4. System persists the todo and returns all data, including readonly fields populated and ownership enforced.
5. If any validation fails, system returns precise reason(s).

### Todo Update
1. User selects their todo and submits changes for allowed fields (`title`, `description`, `dueDate`, `isCompleted`).
2. System validates user ownership, applies field- and lifecycle-level rules.
3. System updates todo and updates `updatedAt` and, if applicable, `completedAt`.
4. If unauthorized or any rule fails, system returns specific error.

### Todo Deletion
1. User selects their own todo for deletion.
2. System confirms ownership and deletes the item.
3. System confirms deletion and returns updated list.
4. If user does not own todo, system denies with error.

### Completion Toggle
1. User sets `isCompleted` true; system sets `completedAt`.
2. User unsets `isCompleted`; system clears `completedAt`.

### Error Flows
- Unauthorized attempts SHALL always be denied.
- Missing or invalid field values lead to error with specific field-focused messages.

## Permission Matrix
| Action      | Owner      | Non-Owner/Anonymous |
|-------------|:----------:|:------------------:|
| Create      |   Yes      | No                 |
| Read/List   |   Yes      | No                 |
| Update      |   Yes      | No                 |
| Delete      |   Yes      | No                 |
| Complete    |   Yes      | No                 |

## Mermaid Diagram: Todo Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph TD
  A["User Authenticated"] --> B["Create Todo"]
  B --> C["Todo Saved (Owner Only)"]
  C --> D["Update/Complete/Delete (Owner Action)"]
  D --> E["(If Completed) Set 'completedAt'"]
  D --> F["(If Deleted) Remove Todo"]
  D --> G["(If Updated) Apply Rules & Update Fields"]
  C -- "Unauthorized Access" --> H["Reject with Error"]
```

## Summary & Acceptance Criteria
- All requirements above SHALL be implemented fully
- All fields and flows SHALL use the constraints/rules expressed above
- System SHALL provide only the minimal viable features with no extras
- No access by non-owners is permitted
- All business rules, validations, and user message expectations are covered here
- Backend developers can implement logic solely from this document, without further clarification or supplemental material

files.reason: To outline future scalability considerations, potential integrations, and roadmap constraints for the todo list application.
keyQuestions: What future changes or growth should be anticipated?
What limitations are known up front?
files.content:
# Future Considerations and Roadmap

## Scalability

The todo list service is designed for sustainable growth and robust user experience as the user base and data requirements increase.

- WHEN user registration rate grows, THE system SHALL handle at least 10,000 monthly active users without noticeable delay in normal usage.
- WHEN up to 5,000 users interact with the service concurrently, THE system SHALL maintain high availability with no degradation of responsiveness in any core feature (adding, deleting, completing todos, or viewing lists).
- WHEN an individual user’s todo list exceeds 1,000 items, THE system SHALL guarantee that all CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations remain responsive and complete within 2 seconds under normal workload.
- WHEN back-end server resource utilization reaches 80%, THE system SHALL immediately notify system operators with infrastructure scaling recommendations and provide automated guidance or triggers for scale-up procedures.
- WHEN spikes in usage occur (e.g., traffic doubles within a short window), THE system SHALL apply rate limiting transparently to burst requests while prioritizing UI stability and user satisfaction—users SHALL always receive feedback if any limit is applied.
- WHEN additional storage or compute power is needed, THE architecture SHALL support horizontal scaling and future distributed deployment.
- WHEN a global user base emerges, THE technical roadmap SHALL include phased plans for regional deployments and data sharding to optimize latency and regulatory compliance.

### Mermaid Diagram - Scalability Handling
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Growth"] --> B{"Resource Adequate?"}
  B -->|"Yes"| C["Normal Processing"]
  B -->|"No"| D["Trigger Scale Up"]
  D --> E["Increase Resources"]
  E --> F["Resume Processing"]
```

## Possible Integrations

- WHEN the system integrates with a calendar service (e.g., Google Calendar, Outlook, or Apple Calendar), THE user SHALL be able to sync individual todo items with external calendar events, including one-way and bi-directional sync modes.
- WHEN notifications for todo deadlines are supported, THE system SHALL provide push, email, and/or SMS reminders for upcoming or overdue tasks, with user-manageable preferences and opt-in controls.
- WHEN collaboration needs arise, THE system SHALL implement workspace or team environments, and users SHALL be able to invite members, assign todos, and share status updates, subject to permission management.
- WHEN more advanced workflows are required, THE system SHALL support third-party automation (such as Zapier or IFTTT) to allow custom triggers and actions tied to todo item creation, completion, or reminder events.
- WHEN users need external reporting or archiving, THE system SHALL permit exports of all personal todo data in CSV or JSON format, with secure authentication before allowing any extract or download process.
- WHEN business analytics partnerships are made, THE system SHALL permit optional, anonymized event tracking to analyze user activity trends, feature adoption, and churn, ensuring compliance with relevant data privacy regulations.

| Integration Area        | Description                                                      |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Calendar Services      | Sync todos with Google/Outlook/Apple calendars                   |
| Notification Services  | Push/email/SMS reminders for due todos                           |
| Collaboration Tools    | Team task sharing via platforms like Slack or MS Teams            |
| File/Data Export       | Download user todo data in CSV/JSON                              |
| Usage Analytics        | Tracking for feature adoption, churn, and usage trends           |


## Known Constraints

- THE system SHALL be launched for individual users only, with every account being personal and private—no shared or collaborative lists or admin roles are available in the MVP.
- WHEN commercial or regulated use is attempted, THE application SHALL clearly state that it is not fit for such scenarios and is intended for personal productivity only.
- WHEN content is created within a todo item, THE input SHALL be limited to text only, with no attachments, sub-tasks, priorities, deadlines, or checklists in the initial release. Each todo SHALL have a simple text title and a completion status.
- WHEN password reset, sign-up, or notification features are used, THE system SHALL depend on availability of external transactional email services. Service interruptions at these providers MAY temporarily delay or prevent critical account operations.
- WHEN an unexpected increase in system load exceeds planned capacity, THE system SHALL enforce rate limiting and, in rare cases, temporarily deny service to new sessions until resource usage returns to acceptable levels, always returning user-friendly status information.
- THE system AND all user-facing content SHALL support English language only; multi-language support is deferred to post-MVP releases.

## Future Feature Ideas

- WHEN collaborative lists become a frequently requested feature, THE system SHALL implement multi-user capability with shareable lists, invitations, and role-based or permission-based access control, all with clear audit trails.
- WHEN feedback indicates user demand for organization, THE system SHALL introduce labels, colored tags, prioritization, and custom filtering for todos.
- WHEN reminders and notifications require more sophistication, THE system SHALL introduce configurable recurring reminders, snoozing, and multiple notification channels per task.
- WHEN users ask for alternative visualizations, THE system SHALL offer calendar and Kanban board views and allow toggling between visualization types for different workflow styles.
- WHEN non-English speaking users reach 10% of the user base or business opportunity is identified, THE system SHALL phase in multi-language/localization support, prioritizing languages based on user adoption.
- WHEN the need for integrations with enterprise collaboration software or file attachments emerges, THE system SHALL evaluate and roll out these features according to a prioritized product roadmap.
- WHEN automation or productivity integration demonstrates clear user value, THE system SHALL add API endpoints for third-party workflow automation.

| Feature                 | Priority   | Trigger for Release                               |
|-------------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Shared/Collaborative Lists | Medium     | User requests/collaboration needs                |
| Custom Labels/Categories   | Medium     | User feedback on task organization               |
| Recurring Reminders       | Medium     | Users require routine scheduling                 |
| Visual Task Management    | Low        | Demand for alternate views of todos              |
| Third-Party Automation    | Low        | Integration value with external platforms        |
| Multi-language Support    | Low        | Substantial non-English user adoption            |


## Summary

The Todo List service is built for robust personal productivity, with scalability at its core and a product roadmap designed for incremental enhancement based on clear business needs and user demand. All MVP constraints, such as single-user operation, English-only support, and text-only todos, shall be strictly observed at launch. As the user base grows and requirements diversify, the system is engineered to anticipate and respond rapidly to new business opportunities, strategic integration requests, and changing compliance or operational needs. Product ownership and development teams should regularly review user feedback and analytics, ensuring ongoing prioritization of scalable, high-value features while preserving simplicity, privacy, and personal utility at every stage of the service evolution.

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
Core registered user entity for the Todo List application.

Stores authentication, identity, and business profile data for each unique account. Includes required credential fields (email, password hash), display name, verification and activation statuses, and timestamps for audit trail and lifecycle management. Serves as the root entity for all user and authentication operations. Every todo belongs to a single user, but todos are managed in separate component tables. Unique email address is strictly enforced, and passwords are stored only as cryptographic hashes.

Deletion means account is permanently erased, with all data removed, and account cannot be recovered.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for user account login. Used as the user's global identifier. Cannot be changed after registration. Must be unique, lowercase, and properly formatted (RFC 5322).

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Salted cryptographically-secure hash of the user's password, never the plain password. Used only for authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Display name for the user, shown in their own UI context. Modifiable by user but unique globally is not enforced.

plainFields.name: is_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the user's email has been successfully verified. Set to true only after email check and activation link consumed.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Indicates if the user account is enabled and usable for logins and business operations. Set to false on permanent or temporary deactivation (e.g., after deletion or security hold).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp, stored in UTC (ISO 8601). Set only at registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last account update (any profile or credential change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Indicates timestamp of permanent account removal. Null if the account is active.

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
Authentication session audit log and context for each user login session.

Tracks every sign-in and session renewal for a user across web/mobile channels, supporting multiple concurrent sessions. Relates to the user as a foreign key. Provides connection metadata (IP, href, referrer), and enables session-level expiry and control. Sessions are necessary for JWT or token life-cycle tracking, session revocation, and security investigations. No soft deletion—expired sessions remain for audit and traceability.

Indexed by (user_id, created_at) for efficient per-user auditing and security monitoring.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to {@link todo_list_users.id}. The account associated with this session.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of session origin (IPv4 or IPv6, as string). Used for risk analysis and audit trails.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Original URL requested at session start/login (may be used for security or analytics).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header value at session start (may be used for tracing session origin).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC-timestamp of session creation (login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: UTC-timestamp when session/token is marked as expired/invalid. Null if still valid.

models.name: todo_list_user_email_verifications
models.description:
Verification events for user account email activation and continued trust.

Records every verification token/email issued and its redemption/expiry process for user email identity. Ensures every authentication email link usage is tracked, enabling repeat verifications, security event tracing, and usage auditing. Contains immutable issued token information, creation/expiration, and redemption metadata. Only tied to users in this component, and all verification lifecycles are distinct rows for security traceability. Used for compliance and prevention of replay attacks.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to {@link todo_list_users.id}. The user account awaiting email verification.

plainFields.name: verification_token
plainFields.description: Secure single-use, randomly-generated string issued for email verification. Must be unique. Set at creation.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Indicates timestamp the verification was successfully consumed (i.e., user activated link). Null if unused or expired.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification offer is no longer valid. Set at creation, immutable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of event creation (when token/email was issued).

models.name: todo_list_user_password_resets
models.description:
Audit log and flow context for password reset requests by users.

Tracks every time a user requests and uses a password reset event, enforcing security best practices (single-use, token expiry, invalidation after use). Enables rate limiting, detects replay or brute force attempts, and preserves an immutable audit trail for account recovery flows.

Tokens are unique, time-limited, and have a one-to-one correspondence with an individual password reset request. Related only to this domain's users. Includes timestamps for creation, expiry, and redemption, with full traceability for compliance, user support, and investigation.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key to {@link todo_list_users.id}. The owner of the password reset process.

plainFields.name: reset_token
plainFields.description: Secure, cryptographically random, single-use token for password reset. Unique per event. Used in password reset link delivery.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was used (password successfully reset). Null if unused/expired.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token/link becomes invalid and may not be used.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset request was initiated.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Table of actionable todo items for users.

This primary business entity stores each individual task a user creates in the minimalist todo application. Every todo is strictly owned by a single user, enforced by a foreign key reference to the user table ({@link todo_list_users.id}).

The table includes all validated business fields: a required, trimmed title; an optional extended description; an optional due date; and completion workflow tracked by 'is_completed' and 'completed_at'.

Temporal columns provide complete auditability for all list operations: creation, update, and completion are timestamped to ISO 8601 UTC. Each row may be accessed and managed only by its owning user, with all access control and CRUD operations enforced at the application/service layer and indexed for query performance.

This table admits no sharing or collaborative features and holds no denormalized or calculated fields. All business logic for todo management, completion toggling, and list UI operations is satisfied via this model and its comprehensive field set. The design guarantees strict data privacy, 3NF normalization, and production-grade scalability in a single-user context.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each todo item, generated as UUID at creation.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owning user who created and may access this todo. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short, required title for the todo item (1–100 characters, trimmed). Must be non-empty and unique only within the business context of the user.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional extended detail for the todo. Maximum 1000 characters; null or empty permitted.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for the todo in ISO 8601 UTC format. Must be present or future if set; null is allowed for floating tasks.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: Completion status of the todo. True if the item is finished, false for pending tasks. Can only be changed by the owner.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was completed. System-managed; set to UTC now when is_completed becomes true, cleared when reverted to incomplete. Null if never completed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: System-managed timestamp for todo creation (ISO 8601 UTC). Readonly to users.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: System-managed timestamp for last modification. Always updated on any change (ISO 8601 UTC). Readonly to users.

### `todo_list_users`

Core registered user entity for the Todo List application.

Stores authentication, identity, and business profile data for each
unique account. Includes required credential fields (email, password
hash), display name, verification and activation statuses, and timestamps
for audit trail and lifecycle management. Serves as the root entity for
all user and authentication operations. Every todo belongs to a single
user, but todos are managed in separate component tables. Unique email
address is strictly enforced, and passwords are stored only as
cryptographic hashes.

Deletion means account is permanently erased, with all data removed, and
account cannot be recovered.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for user account login. Used as the user's global
  > identifier. Cannot be changed after registration. Must be unique,
  > lowercase, and properly formatted (RFC 5322).
- `password_hash`
  > Salted cryptographically-secure hash of the user's password, never the
  > plain password. Used only for authentication.
- `display_name`
  > Display name for the user, shown in their own UI context. Modifiable by
  > user but unique globally is not enforced.
- `is_verified`
  > Indicates whether the user's email has been successfully verified. Set to
  > true only after email check and activation link consumed.
- `is_active`
  > Indicates if the user account is enabled and usable for logins and
  > business operations. Set to false on permanent or temporary deactivation
  > (e.g., after deletion or security hold).
- `created_at`
  > Account creation timestamp, stored in UTC (ISO 8601). Set only at
  > registration.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last account update (any profile or credential change).
- `deleted_at`
  > Indicates timestamp of permanent account removal. Null if the account is
  > active.

### `todo_list_user_sessions`

Authentication session audit log and context for each user login session.

Tracks every sign-in and session renewal for a user across web/mobile
channels, supporting multiple concurrent sessions. Relates to the user as
a foreign key. Provides connection metadata (IP, href, referrer), and
enables session-level expiry and control. Sessions are necessary for JWT
or token life-cycle tracking, session revocation, and security
investigations. No soft deletion—expired sessions remain for audit and
traceability.

Indexed by (user_id, created_at) for efficient per-user auditing and
security monitoring.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`
  > Foreign key to [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users). The account associated with
  > this session.
- `ip`
  > IP address of session origin (IPv4 or IPv6, as string). Used for risk
  > analysis and audit trails.
- `href`
  > Original URL requested at session start/login (may be used for security
  > or analytics).
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header value at session start (may be used for tracing
  > session origin).
- `created_at`: UTC-timestamp of session creation (login time).
- `expired_at`
  > UTC-timestamp when session/token is marked as expired/invalid. Null if
  > still valid.

### `todo_list_user_email_verifications`

Verification events for user account email activation and continued trust.

Records every verification token/email issued and its redemption/expiry
process for user email identity. Ensures every authentication email link
usage is tracked, enabling repeat verifications, security event tracing,
and usage auditing. Contains immutable issued token information,
creation/expiration, and redemption metadata. Only tied to users in this
component, and all verification lifecycles are distinct rows for security
traceability. Used for compliance and prevention of replay attacks.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`
  > Foreign key to [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users). The user account awaiting
  > email verification.
- `verification_token`
  > Secure single-use, randomly-generated string issued for email
  > verification. Must be unique. Set at creation.
- `consumed_at`
  > Indicates timestamp the verification was successfully consumed (i.e.,
  > user activated link). Null if unused or expired.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when the verification offer is no longer valid. Set at
  > creation, immutable.
- `created_at`: UTC timestamp of event creation (when token/email was issued).

### `todo_list_user_password_resets`

Audit log and flow context for password reset requests by users.

Tracks every time a user requests and uses a password reset event,
enforcing security best practices (single-use, token expiry, invalidation
after use). Enables rate limiting, detects replay or brute force
attempts, and preserves an immutable audit trail for account recovery
flows.

Tokens are unique, time-limited, and have a one-to-one correspondence
with an individual password reset request. Related only to this domain's
users. Includes timestamps for creation, expiry, and redemption, with
full traceability for compliance, user support, and investigation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`
  > Foreign key to [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users). The owner of the password
  > reset process.
- `reset_token`
  > Secure, cryptographically random, single-use token for password reset.
  > Unique per event. Used in password reset link delivery.
- `consumed_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset token was used (password successfully
  > reset). Null if unused/expired.
- `expires_at`: Timestamp when the reset token/link becomes invalid and may not be used.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the reset request was initiated.

### `todo_list_todos`

Table of actionable todo items for users.

This primary business entity stores each individual task a user creates
in the minimalist todo application. Every todo is strictly owned by a
single user, enforced by a foreign key reference to the user table
([todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users)).

The table includes all validated business fields: a required, trimmed
title; an optional extended description; an optional due date; and
completion workflow tracked by 'is_completed' and 'completed_at'.

Temporal columns provide complete auditability for all list operations:
creation, update, and completion are timestamped to ISO 8601 UTC. Each
row may be accessed and managed only by its owning user, with all access
control and CRUD operations enforced at the application/service layer and
indexed for query performance.

This table admits no sharing or collaborative features and holds no
denormalized or calculated fields. All business logic for todo
management, completion toggling, and list UI operations is satisfied via
this model and its comprehensive field set. The design guarantees strict
data privacy, 3NF normalization, and production-grade scalability in a
single-user context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary Key. Unique identifier for each todo item, generated as UUID at
  > creation.
- `todo_list_user_id`
  > Owning user who created and may access this todo. {@link
  > todo_list_users.id}.
- `title`
  > Short, required title for the todo item (1–100 characters, trimmed). Must
  > be non-empty and unique only within the business context of the user.
- `description`
  > Optional extended detail for the todo. Maximum 1000 characters; null or
  > empty permitted.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for the todo in ISO 8601 UTC format. Must be present or
  > future if set; null is allowed for floating tasks.
- `is_completed`
  > Completion status of the todo. True if the item is finished, false for
  > pending tasks. Can only be changed by the owner.
- `completed_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was completed. System-managed; set to UTC now
  > when is_completed becomes true, cleared when reverted to incomplete. Null
  > if never completed.
- `created_at`
  > System-managed timestamp for todo creation (ISO 8601 UTC). Readonly to
  > users.
- `updated_at`
  > System-managed timestamp for last modification. Always updated on any
  > change (ISO 8601 UTC). Readonly to users.

operations.specification: User registration endpoint for the Todo List service. Associates with the 'todo_list_users' table. The flow creates a new user record (requires a unique email and password), and sets 'is_verified' to false. On success, issues a verification email, blocks login until verification, and creates a pending user. This operation is public, does not require prior authentication, and is the entry point for new user onboarding. Email is globally unique and never modifiable. Password is stored as a secure hash and never returned.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables registration for new users by accepting a unique email address and password. The registration process involves strict email uniqueness enforcement—if a duplicate is detected in the 'todo_list_users' table, the system will reject the registration with a conflict error (referencing the 'email' unique index). The user's account is created in a pending (unverified) state, and a verification email is sent to the provided address using a unique token.

Only after verifying the email (using a separate operation) will the account become active (see 'is_verified' and 'is_active' fields in 'todo_list_users'). The password is securely stored as a salted cryptographic hash in 'password_hash' and never returned.

Upon successful registration, further authentication is blocked until email verification is completed. Users cannot change the email after registration, as enforced by the immutable 'email' column.

This registration operation is related to the email verification process, which users must complete before being able to log in.

Unsuccessful attempts due to invalid input or existing email result in clear error messages, following the validation rules established in the schema. Only user-facing data is returned—never internal account or security metadata.
operations.summary: Registers a new user in the todo_list_users table (pending verification).

requestBody.description: Registration payload, including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user info for verified or pending user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: join

operations.specification: User login endpoint for the Todo List service. Operates on the 'todo_list_users' table for credential checks. Accepts email and password, verifies the account is active and 'is_verified' is true, then authenticates. On success, returns new JWT access and refresh tokens. Fails if credentials are invalid or account is not verified. Login is blocked until registration and email verification operations are fully completed. No user profile is returned except minimal token and identifying data.
operations.description:
Handles user login, validating submitted credentials against the 'todo_list_users' table using the combination of 'email' and securely-hashed 'password_hash' values. Only users marked as both 'is_verified' and 'is_active' can successfully receive tokens. The endpoint denies authentication if credentials are incorrect, if the email has not been verified, or the account is deactivated.

The operation returns JWT access and refresh tokens for valid users, leveraging the account's unique ID, and does not expose any internal security data or hashed passwords. Login requires that the email correspond to an existing, verified account in the user table.

The endpoint distinguishes only between correct and incorrect credentials, using generic error messages to prevent user enumeration or disclosing security-sensitive information.

Related operations include registration (for creating a pending account) and email verification (to activate the user).

Multiple concurrent sessions are supported via the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table, with each session generating its own tracked row for audit and security analysis.
operations.summary: Authenticates verified user from todo_list_users and issues tokens.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user info for authenticated user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Token refresh operation for the Todo List service. Operates on existing valid refresh tokens tied to user sessions (see 'todo_list_user_sessions' table). Accepts a currently valid refresh token, validates it against the session log, and, if correct and not expired or revoked, issues new access/refresh tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, missing, or expired, authentication is denied. Token life cycle and session management are tied to the user account and session log for security traceability.
operations.description:
Allows users to obtain a new access token by submitting a valid, unexpired refresh token. The operation cross-checks the provided token against the active session records in 'todo_list_user_sessions', confirming that the token is active, not expired ('expired_at' is null or in the future), and properly assigned to the user session indicated.

Session audits are enforced at the database level, tying each refresh token to its session and preventing reuse after logout or expiration. Expired, invalid, or missing tokens result in authentication failure. All critical information—such as token lifetime, IP, session metadata—is managed in the session log.

Refresh operations are central to secure, long-lived user authentication in stateless environments. No user profile or business data is returned except new token(s).

This endpoint is expected to be called by clients automatically on access token expiry. Failures trigger re-authentication via the login operation.
operations.summary: Issues new tokens for users with valid refresh tokens via todo_list_user_sessions.

requestBody.description: The valid refresh token to be exchanged for new tokens.

responseBody.description: Updated authentication tokens and user info for re-authenticated user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Handles user email verification flow. Uses 'todo_list_user_email_verifications' table. Accepts the unique verification token sent to user's email, checks if it has not expired or been previously consumed, and if valid, marks the user as 'is_verified' and enables login. Prevents login until verification is complete. If the token is invalid, expired, or already used, blocks activation and provides a suitable error message. This endpoint finalizes the user onboarding and switches the user's account from pending to active.
operations.description:
This endpoint accepts the email verification token (found in the 'todo_list_user_email_verifications' table) and, if valid, activates the associated user's account (sets 'is_verified' to true). Upon redemption, the 'consumed_at' timestamp is set, and the user's status transitions from pending to active, enabling the login operation.

If the verification token does not exist, has already been used ('consumed_at' not null), or is expired, the action is denied and the user remains unable to log in. Each verification token is single-use and time-limited, referencing the 'expires_at' and 'consumed_at' columns for validity.

This operation completes new user onboarding after registration. Invalid or expired tokens result in clear error messages, promoting security and usability.

Related operations are registration (creates the token), and login (requires successful verification before tokens are issued).

Failure scenarios cover incorrect usage and timeouts, maintaining auditability via the verification events log.
operations.summary: Finalizes user registration by activating account via email token in todo_list_user_email_verifications.

requestBody.description: Payload containing the email verification token.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating email verification success or failure.

operations.name: verifyEmail

operations.specification: User password reset request operation, tracking and handling via 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. Accepts email, issues a secure time-limited reset token if the account exists (does not reveal account presence), and delivers it to the user via email. Used when a user forgets their password. Never returns user account data; always responds generically regardless of presence. Rate limits enforced via resets log.
operations.description:
Initiates a password reset for user accounts. The endpoint accepts an email address and, if the corresponding user is present in 'todo_list_users', generates a unique single-use reset token (persisted in 'todo_list_user_password_resets'). This token is sent to the email on record. No information is leaked about whether the email exists, always replying success to prevent user enumeration.

All requests are audited; excessive attempts can be rate-limited using the password resets schema. The reset token includes strict expiration ('expires_at') and is unique per reset event ('reset_token').

The reset process itself is completed in a separate endpoint, where the user redeems the token by setting a new password.

Failed or expired token submissions handled in a companion operation.

Related entities: user (identity), resets (event log, token issue).

This operation never reveals presence of non-existent accounts for privacy and security reasons.
operations.summary: Initiates password reset process for user by generating time-limited reset token (todo_list_user_password_resets).

requestBody.description: Payload with user's email address for password reset request.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating reset initiation (never reveals account presence).

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Completes user password reset flow using 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. Accepts reset token and new password, validates and consumes the token if valid, and updates the user's password in 'todo_list_users' (hashing it securely). Token is single-use and must not be expired or previously redeemed. On success, provides minimal confirmation. On failure, gives generic error to prevent abuse or enumeration.
operations.description:
Redemption endpoint for password reset: accepts the one-time reset token (from 'todo_list_user_password_resets') along with a new password. If the token is present, unconsumed, and not expired, the associated user's password is updated to the securely-hashed new value in 'todo_list_users', and the reset token event is marked as consumed ('consumed_at').

Used tokens cannot be re-used, and expired ones are rejected. Password reset is a sensitive operation and is audited in the event log for traceability, allowing enforcement of security/compliance policies.

Failing this operation (invalid or expired token) triggers a generic error message, preventing attackers from probing for valid tokens or emails.

Related flow requires a prior password reset initiation request, logged in the password resets table, and enforces the single-use, time-limited guarantee via database schema constraints.
operations.summary: Updates user's password via valid reset token in todo_list_user_password_resets; single-use only.

requestBody.description: Payload containing reset token and new password.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating password reset result.

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.specification: Authenticated endpoint for changing a user's password. Requires current (old) password and new password. Operates on 'todo_list_users' - verifies old password matches 'password_hash', then applies the update after securely hashing the new password. Fails if old password is incorrect. It operates on the todo_list_user_password_resets table, providing security and audit transparency by allowing users to see if and when password reset links were generated, expired, or redeemed for their account. This supports user-driven security review, suspicious activity detection, and transparency over past and active reset flows. Filtering, pagination, and sorting are supported to navigate large histories.
operations.summary: Retrieve password reset history for the authenticated user's account using the password reset log table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an authenticated user to query the log of all password reset requests and their status for their own account. Results include events whether used, expired, or still active. The operation supports filtering by date range, token status (expired/used/active), and is ordered by creation time for ease of review.

Security is critical: only the owner of the account may access their own password reset event history. The operation relies on user identity provided by authentication context, not a path parameter, so no sensitive user ID is directly exchanged or exposed. Rate limiting is enforced to prevent probing, and data is filtered strictly for the authenticated user only.

This history is sourced from the todo_list_user_password_resets table. Each item includes timestamps for issuance, expiry, and redemption/consumption. This operation can be used in account security dashboards, help users recognize unwanted resets, and provide a compliance trail for security events. Related operations: GET /users/me/passwordResets/{resetToken} for inspecting a single reset event in detail.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for password reset event history on the user's account.

responseBody.description: Paginated and filterable list of the user's password reset history, including each event's status and metadata.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific password reset event for the authenticated user. It operates on a single event from the todo_list_user_password_resets table, identified by its unique reset token. It confirms ownership, presents all relevant timestamps, and allows the user to check whether the link is still active, when it was created, when it will expire, and if it has already been consumed. This is essential for self-service auditing, helping users to validate and investigate password reset events.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for a password reset event by token for the user's account using the password reset log table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows the authenticated user to inspect the details of a password reset event from their own account by specifying the event's unique reset token in the path. Information returned includes creation, expiration, and consumption timestamps, as well as verification that the reset token belongs to the querying user and has not been used or expired.

Strict security and privacy controls are enforced: only the user who owns the reset token may access its event details, and tokens are checked for validity, expiration, and ownership. The token parameter does not expose the internal reset event ID, but is a single-use, cryptographically strong identifier.

The operation references the todo_list_user_password_resets table, returning all related event information for UI display or suspicious activity review. If the token is invalid or no longer associated with the authenticated user, a not-found or error response is returned. Related operation: PATCH /users/me/passwordResets for listing all events.

parameters.name: resetToken
parameters.description: Unique, single-use password reset token for identifying the reset event (scoped to the authenticated user).

responseBody.description: Password reset event information, including metadata and security-related timestamps.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation provides advanced searching and retrieval of todo list items across all users, supporting filtering, pagination, and sorting. It operates on the todo_list_todos table in the Prisma schema, leveraging all defined fields for precise querying. The search capabilities are designed for flexibility, enabling queries by text, completion state, due date ranges, and linked user. Results are paginated and may be sorted by various attributes as defined in business requirements.
operations.description:
Search and filter todo list items matching user-supplied criteria with support for pagination and flexible sorting.

This endpoint enables users and admins to retrieve lists of todo items, specifying criteria such as completion status, associated user, and time range.

Security and filtering considerations are implemented according to the requesting user's role and permissions. Only items visible or accessible to the user will be returned. Pagination prevents overloading responses, while input validation and error handling protect against malformed queries or constraint violations.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of todo items from todo_list_todos table

requestBody.description: Search and filtering parameters for todo items (completion state, user, query, pagination, etc.)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo item summaries matching the search criteria, as defined in ITodoListTodo.ISummary.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information for a specific todo item, identified by its unique ID. It interacts directly with the todo_list_todos table in the Prisma schema. The endpoint ensures that users can view only items they are authorized to access, enforcing appropriate filtering by user or permissions as applicable.
operations.description:
Obtain full detail for a specific todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint is designed to provide complete information for a particular todo item, including all fields and metadata stored in the database. Permissions and access control ensure that only authorized users can retrieve this information.

The response structure complies with the ITodoListTodo data model, providing clients with all attributes necessary for viewing, editing, or auditing the todo item. Error responses handle cases where the todo item does not exist or access is denied.
operations.summary: Retrieve complete details about a specific todo item by ID from todo_list_todos table

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID format, as defined by todo_list_todos schema)

responseBody.description: Full todo item details as defined in ITodoListTodo.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item in the todo_list_todos table. It allows an authenticated user to generate a unique, actionable task with required title and optional detail fields. Each todo is strictly owned by the creating user, linked through a mandatory foreign key to todo_list_users. All business validation rules for fields such as title trim length, permissible due date (present/future), and correct data types are enforced at the application layer before persisting the entity. Temporal system fields including creation, update, and (if relevant) completion timestamps are set automatically. The response returns the newly created todo with all metadata, ensuring immediate feedback and seamless UI updates for the user.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the current authenticated user. The operation requires at minimum a trimmed, non-empty title between 1 and 100 characters, which must be unique within the user's list for business logic clarity, though not enforced at the database level.

Optionally, the user may specify a description (up to 1000 characters) and a due date restricted to the present or future (ISO 8601 UTC format). Initial completion status is always false unless explicitly provided; completed_at must be null at creation. All timestamps (created_at/updated_at) are generated by the system upon insertion.

Authentication is mandatory, and the creating user is assigned as the owner via the session/user principal without needing to pass a user ID in the request. Immediate error responses are produced for invalid title length, improperly formatted due dates, or attempts to create todos for other users. This endpoint is the standard entry for all todo creation workflows in the system.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item in todo_list_todos.

requestBody.description: Information necessary to create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all metadata and owner linkage.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item owned by the current authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table. The endpoint facilitates editing of core business fields such as title, description, due_date, and toggling of is_completed. Field-level business logic is enforced, including validation of title length, description length, date format, and is_completed state transitions. Timestamps for updated_at (system-managed) and completed_at (system-managed for is_completed transition) are applied automatically, supporting UI synchronization and auditability. The update is restricted to the owner, with user context determined implicitly from authentication without explicit user ID fields in the request or path. The response returns the updated todo item reflecting all new values.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item belonging to the authenticated user. The todoId parameter uniquely identifies the target todo, which must be owned by the requesting user, preventing unauthorized access or edits.

Field updates may include a new title (validated for trim and length), a description (up to 1000 characters), a due date (present or future, ISO 8601 format), and changes to completion status (is_completed and completed_at handled automatically). System-managed columns updated_at and, if applicable, completed_at are set at the time of update by the service logic. Any transition of is_completed from false to true also updates completed_at; resetting to false clears it.

Attempting to update a todo not owned by the user, or passing invalid field data (e.g., too long title/description, invalid dates, unauthorized changes to other users' todos) results in a clear error. All validation rules reflect the strict requirements and privacy model of the todo_list_todos schema.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo item in todo_list_todos by unique todoId.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to update.

requestBody.description: Fields and values to update for the specified todo item.

responseBody.description: The updated todo item with all current business and audit fields.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created before it can be updated. The 'todoId' required for update is generated by the creation operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a single todo item from the system. It maps directly to the todo_list_todos table in the database. The operation deletes the todo specified by its unique identifier, provided as the path parameter. Deletion is allowed only by the owning user, and strict access control is enforced; only the user that owns the todo can erase it. All fields, including audit timestamps, are removed from persistence with this action. There is no soft-delete or archival mechanism—removal is a true data deletion per the schema, conforming to the single-user privacy focus of the todo list app.

Error conditions include attempting to delete a todo that does not exist or does not belong to the requesting user, in which cases appropriate error responses (404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden) are issued. This endpoint should be called only when the user intentionally wants to irreversibly erase a todo from their private set. Other CRUD actions (create, update, read) should be performed via the corresponding endpoints.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item that belongs to the authenticated user. This endpoint directly erases the specified todo from the todo_list_todos table.

Only the owner of the todo is permitted to perform this operation. Authentication and authorization must be enforced at the application layer to guarantee that each user can manage only their own todos. Attempting to access or delete another user's todo will result in a forbidden error.

Upon successful deletion, all information for the deleted todo is immediately and irreversibly removed from persistent storage. This action does not support recovery, soft delete, or undo. Auditability is provided by the system's timestamping prior to deletion, but the record itself will not exist after this operation. If the todo does not exist or the id is invalid, a 404 Not Found error is returned.

This operation should be used when the user intends to irreversibly remove a task from their todo list, such as to clean up completed or abandoned tasks. It is recommended to confirm user intent in the UI before invoking this endpoint, as recovery is impossible post-deletion.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item from the todo_list_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo to delete (UUID format).

operations.name: erase

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: A registered user who can create, view, update, complete, and delete their own todo items. Can register, authenticate, and manage only their own account and todos.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.
